title: Cohort Retention and Churn Rate Analysis
description: Tracking longitudinal customer or patient engagement decay curves across discrete onboarding cohorts.
conditions: Subscription, recurring engagement, or longitudinal therapy datasets
Need to evaluate whether product/service retention is improving over successive generations
recommended_methods: Cohort Retention Heatmap matrix (Acquisition Month vs Months Since Onboarding)
Kaplan-Meier survival curve estimation for time-to-churn distribution
Hazard rate modeling via Cox Proportional Hazards regression
selection_rules: Calculate retention rate strictly as: Active_Users_Month_N / Total_Users_Cohort_Month_0
If retention curve flattens into a horizontal asymptote, product has achieved baseline product-market fit
Use Cox Proportional Hazards regression to discover which customer onboarding features predict lower churn risk
limitations: Recent cohorts suffer from right-censoring (insufficient elapsed time to evaluate long-term retention)
Defining 'churn' in non-contractual business models requires arbitrary inactivity window cutoffs
